summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -6 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar −; brl −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +2.5%; weakest: Sugar #11 -13.2%. Key releases ahead: US Fed Chairman Warsh Speaks (11-16 12:00 PM ET); US Core Retail Sales m/m (11-17 8:30 AM ET); US Retail Sales m/m (11-17 8:30 AM ET); US FOMC Meeting Minutes (11-18 2:00 PM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.12% (+3 bp in a month), 2-year 4.83% (+9 bp); 2s10s curve +29 bp (-6 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.12% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.59 (+1.7% in a month, +5.4% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.786 (+13.5% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.654 (-0.6%); USD/MXN 18.51 (+0.4%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -3.2% in a month (+8.3% YTD); VIX 22.9. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 85.06 $/bbl (-14.1% in a month), Brent 91.84, ULSD 4.058 $/gal (-14.1%), natural gas 3.12 (-7.8%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -8.9% in a month, Shanghai Composite -3.1%, Hang Seng -1.8%, yuan +0.6% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 8 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (24%); S&P GSCI -10.6% in a month; gold -7.7%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
